issues.cell: commit's 'as it began' and 'newly' x law 1 (9), (10) x law 4's undo and dependents x section 7.4 Independence (veto 21, 23; W11; T110-4 (c); V09's Go back to here, T-V9-16)
issues.claim: An undo or redo is one commit, so it makes 'newly' every line, band or soffit it restores. A wall drawn across an aqueduct's vault-use span, the aqueduct then shape-locked, the wall deleted, ctrl+Z (or a viaduct over a ring shape-locked since and deleted; or a wall in a placement-locked building's strip; or a clerk/host group [meeting, lock] undone and redone; or Go back to here across such a triple): law 1 (10) or (9) is false at the undo's end, yet law 4 names only later live events as dependents and the lock precedes the target, so there is none. Builder A applies it (section 7.4 passes) and section 5.3's row aborts E_INVARIANT; Builder B refuses refuse.undo.dependent naming nothing; Builder C reads newly against the target's record and applies it (W11, veto 21) - while veto 23 refuses it and T110-4 (c) has no correct build. Pass 6's dateless 'newly' opened the class (PRB7F-LCK-01 decided only a lock made after the target).
issues.required_change: Part L, commit: after 'it makes newly, whatever order its fields hold' add '- save that an undo or a redo, the exact inverse or re-application of its target (law 4), makes newly only what differs from the state its target's record gives (an undo: as its target began; a redo: as it ended, a group's at its last event's end), a meeting it re-creates with a structure or a lock that a later live event laid or made counting as made newly (law 4's dependents)'. Law 1 (9)'s gloss: add 'and so does one an undo or a redo brings back as it stood under a lock no later live event made (commit)'. Veto 21: 'across what was built since is refused' -> 'across what was built or locked since is refused, naming the edits to undo first; one that brings back what stood lawfully under a lock made before its target applies'.

issues.cell: commit's 'newly' ('a line, band or strip where none lay') x law 1 (9), (10) (a relation) x the check's '(9) - (11) by what the commit made newly or moved' x Order's kept crossing x law 4's (G2) last clause; W2, W14
issues.claim: Law 1 (9) and (10) bar relations (a wall's line in a held building's strip; a line, band or strip across a shape-locked raised way's vault-use span) while 'newly' is defined per point. (1) A ring laid before an aqueduct's shape lock crosses its already-open vault-use span (no chamber), and the user re-grades it light -> full within that span's strip, or nudges its crossing 1 m within it; or nudges a wall already in a locked building's strip further away: per point the moved line or wider band lies where none lay, so the edit is refused (or a village REPLACEMENT waits); per meeting the held thing takes nothing new and the edit applies. (2) A re-grade whose wider band grows the held building's strip (widened by the wall's strips' width) onto the wall's unmoved line, its band and strips still off the span's own strip: per point lawful (no line laid or moved), per meeting newly in the strip and re-traced out of it, else refused. Two maps per gesture.
issues.required_change: Part L, commit: after 'it makes newly, whatever order its fields hold' add '- read per meeting: a meeting is made newly where its two structures did not meet so as the commit began (a wall's line, band or strip in a span's strip or a held building's strip it did not lie in, a run and a deck line that did not cross, a merge or a cap where none was), whichever side moved or grew, and deepened where a reading at a meeting that stood becomes deeper (a soffit lower over a point of the run, a merge or a cap over a point it did not cover, a vault span read open); a meeting that stood and stands, its lines moved or widened within the same strips and crossings and no reading deeper, is neither'. The check: '(9) - (11) by what the commit made newly or moved, against what stood as it began' -> '(9) and (10) by the meetings the commit made newly or deepened (commit), (11) by what it moved or removed, each against what stood as it began'.

issues.cell: Carried way ('by hand section 7.3's S7 operator makes its gate ... a placement-locked one too') x section 7.3's S7 row (re-trace the run between the nearest unaffected towers) x Placement ('its line's vertices') x the check's (10) x law 2 (b) ('Never ... a Tier-2 structure's line'); E-S2; PRB7F-LCK-02's closure
issues.claim: A raised road into a placement-locked town (E-S2's fixture): Carried way makes the gate by section 7.3's S7 operator, whose row re-traces the run between the nearest unaffected towers and makes the gate at a junction that is a vertex of the trace (Gate.junction; section 7.1's T3 row: a gate's crossing is a trace vertex). Placement is 'a wall-like structure's trace (its line's vertices) ... (a gate newly laid moving none)', and the check compares 'the fields of its placement ... unchanged unless the event names it'. Builder A compares fields: the ring's vertex list changed by an op not naming it - E_INVARIANT on every raised road into a placement-locked town; Builder B reads the line's geometry, the junction part of the gate's place - passes (PRB7F-LCK-02's 'no field of its placement changes'). For any wall, the re-trace re-lays a run of the standing, older Tier-2 wall, which law 2 never moves at a meeting, lawful only if it reproduces the line - which no text says.
issues.required_change: Part L, Carried way: 'makes its gate in every wall the declared way crosses, a placement-locked one too (a gate the op lays, ...' -> '... a placement-locked one too - inserting the gate at the crossing on the run's standing line, the run neither re-traced nor moved, its other vertices, towers and gates kept - (a gate the op lays, ...'. Placement: '(a gate newly laid moving none; ...)' -> '(a gate newly laid moving none, and the vertex its junction inserts on the line changing no field of placement; ...)'. The check: 'unchanged unless the event names it as its own target' -> 'unchanged - a vertex a newly laid gate's junction inserts on the line excepted - unless the event names it as its own target'.

issues.cell: the Terms' lead (every strip a wall is kept from the union of every standing raised way's) x law 1 (4)'s band clause ('a raised way's strip only to cross its deck line - entering on one long side, leaving by the other, meeting the deck line once there') x the bent-group sentence's Several raised ways
issues.claim: Two raised ways whose strips meet - a declared viaduct beside an aqueduct with decks 1.5 m apart (strips widened by stripMarginM overlap), or an elevated road crossing over an aqueduct by a ring - and a hand wall (or a dragged run) crossing both. On the Terms' union, the band enters once and meets two deck lines, so 'meeting the deck line once' is false and the stroke is bent to where the strips part, else refused; where the decks cross the union has no 'long sides' and (4) has no reading. Read raised way by raised way, as the bent-group sentence's Several raised ways does ('the rule holds for each'), the stroke is lawful as drawn. Two maps, or none, by canvas and clerk (the clerk's points form searches only shapes law 1 admits). The clause is pass 6's (PRB7F-LCK-05).
issues.required_change: Part L, law 1 (4): 'and its band lies in a raised way's strip only to cross its deck line - entering on one long side, leaving by the other, meeting the deck line once there' -> 'and, for each raised way, its band lies in that raised way's own strip only to cross that raised way's deck line - entering on one long side of that strip, leaving by the other, meeting that deck line once there - whatever other raised way's strip it lies in there (the Terms' union read raised way by raised way in this clause)'.

issues.cell: law 1 (10)'s 'save as the other side's own condition changes (a fall, decay, ruin or repair)' x law 1 (7) x Entry ('no soft reading from a meeting made or deepened after its lock') x veto 23 x J147 (3); C10
issues.claim: A ring runs beneath a viaduct, capped at span s; s falls (a hazard, or the user's hand convert breach), the ring's top back up; the user shape-locks the ring; then repairs s by hand (convert repairRaised, or C10's new raised part over a cleared support). Law 1 (10)'s exception admits the repair as the other side's condition change, so the ring's top and walk are cut to the soffit after its lock. J147 (3), the owner's rule: 'the shape-locked wall never changes; the newer thing bends itself, else gives way (by hand refused ...)'; Entry and veto 23 ('what it read from meetings that stood when it was locked follows them') agree - no cap stood at the lock. Builder A applies the repair (the law's exception); Builder B refuses it (Entry, J147). Pass 5 admitted a repair for 'the readings it had' at the lock (PRB7E-TIM-04); pass 6's rewording dropped 'it had'.
issues.required_change: Part L, law 1 (10): 'save as the other side's own condition changes (a fall, decay, ruin or repair) or a frame growth re-derives its end span, its readings then following what stands' -> 'save as the other side's own condition changes - a fall, decay or ruin, or a repair restoring a part that stood over or across it when it was locked - or a frame growth re-derives its end span, its readings then following what stands; a repair or a new raised part (C10) that would give it a reading it did not have when it was locked makes a meeting deeper after its lock (by hand refused, at an epoch waiting: law 2 (c))'. Veto 23: after 'a vault laid again or a top back up when the other side goes' add 'and a repaired span bringing back only what stood when it was locked'.

issues.cell: law 2 (a)'s search list ('a castle's siting') x its given list ('a moved vertex or grip, ... an edit's value') x law 3 key (2)'s drag clause; the fixed-place sentence's castle by hand; PRB7C-LCK-04; E-D4
issues.claim: An on_enceinte castle's keep grip (setAttr(castle, 'site', point)) or bailey handle (setAttr(castle, 'baileyArea', ...)) dragged so that a weld vertex, or the town-side gate on every side, falls in a road deck's zone (law 1 (6)). Law 2 (a) names it both a search ('a castle's siting', its own cost choosing among lawful claims) and a given shape ('a moved vertex or grip ... an edit's value', law 3's nearest). Builder A (PRB7C-LCK-04's 'A castle dragged is a siting ... a search') re-sites the claim by the siting's ranking, wherever it ranks best; Builder B (the fixed-place sentence's 'its claim moving whole to the nearest lawful site') moves it whole to the nearest lawful site, measured back along the keep's drag (key (2)), and bends a bailey area to the nearest lawful value. Two castles for one gesture, by canvas and clerk; E-D4's 'in reach' splits the same way.
issues.required_change: Part L, law 2 (a): 'an op that searches for its shape - a pull or cost field, a route solve, a castle's siting, ...' -> '... a castle's siting at generation, a regeneration or an epoch, ...'; and 'an op given its shape - a stroke, a moved vertex or grip, ...' -> 'an op given its shape - a stroke, a moved vertex or grip (a castle's keep grip or bailey handle, its claim moved whole or its area bent, among them), ...'.
